statusVocabulary.BLOCKED: Cannot start or finish until a named dependency clears, or until an accountable party decides.
statusVocabulary.READY: Everything this repository must supply exists and is verified. Execution is outside the repository.
statusVocabulary.SPECIFIED_NOT_APPLIED: A complete, test-passing artifact exists here. It has not been applied to the tenant.
statusVocabulary.EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE: Cannot be built without information this repository does not hold.
statusVocabulary.DECISION_REQUIRED: No technical blocker. Waiting on a person to decide.
statusVocabulary.ACCEPTED: Known, reasoned, and deliberately not being changed.
statusVocabulary.APPLIED_UNVERIFIED: Executed against the tenant, with a run record naming the evidence. Not the same as resolved: the item's own resolution criteria say what still has to be observed before it closes.
statusVocabulary.DISCHARGED_UNTRACKABLE: Done, evidenced once, and permanently unverifiable from this repository — because the proof is deliberately not in it. This is the terminal case of APPLIED_UNVERIFIED: not "not verified yet" but "cannot be verified here, by design". Reserved for work whose only artifact is a credential or a git-ignored file, which credential hygiene requires be destroyed or never committed. Counts as CLOSED. A gate reading this repository will go on reporting such an item as outstanding in every clone, forever; that is expected, is not a regression, and the gate must say so rather than leave a reader to re-raise it.
statusVocabulary.RESOLVED: The item's own resolution criteria are met, with the evidence named. Kept in the register rather than deleted, so the record of what was decided and why survives.

items.title: No server-side enforcement is running anywhere
items.sourceRegister: STATUS_REPORT.md finding G-04 (Partial); npm run commission — WARNINGS
items.description: The authenticating proxy that would have validated tokens, derived roles and authorised actions was built and then removed rather than deployed. Every obligation it carried now belongs to each flow individually: token validation, role derivation, per-action authorisation, rate limiting, reference minting, upload ticketing and the filename policy. Caller identity is a client-asserted userEmail read from localStorage. SHARPENED 2026-09-24. 'No server-side enforcement is running anywhere' understated this rather than overstating it. FETCH_ALL was BUILT with the whole chain — caller, directory lookup, role, role permissions, a permission expression and a condition — and then the condition was wired to a constant, so the chain runs, computes the right answer, and is ignored. ITEM-61 carries that with the run record. The obligation this item names is therefore not merely unbuilt in one place; it was built, disconnected, and nothing noticed for at least five days. And the deeper half of this item stands unchanged even once ITEM-61 is fixed: Compose_FetchAll_Caller takes the caller's address from the REQUEST BODY, so a restored expression authorises whoever the caller claims to be. Enforcement anchored on an unauthenticated identity is what this estate has, not none — which is a sharper statement of the same problem, not a smaller one. BUILT 2026-09-24, NOT YET APPLIED. The obligation this item names is now implemented in the artefacts the operator pastes into the tenant, and the status moves from BLOCKED to SPECIFIED_NOT_APPLIED because what was missing was a design and what is missing now is an application. The blocker was narrower than 'no enforcement exists' and was not visible until the flows were read: NOTHING MINTED A PROOF. IP_OTP_VERIFY answered verificationToken: 'optional-server-issued-token' — a literal placeholder — so §2 obligation 1, verify the proof, had nothing to verify, and core/otp-identity.js refused the response for carrying no token, which means internal sign-in could not complete at all. The portal half had the whole mechanism already: scripts/build-designer-paste.mjs mints a row in the shared proof ledger on verification and reads it back on every governed write, checking unconsumed and unexpired. Both halves are now built on that one ledger. OTP_VERIFY mints — an opaque token, the directory address, Purpose internal-session, and §2a's approved four-hour internal lifetime read from a single expression so the row and the client cannot disagree by microseconds — and returns the token the client already knows how to read. Six internal endpoints — FETCH_ALL, GET_DOCS, REFERENCE_DATA, SINGLE_ASSIGNMENT, BULK_ASSIGNMENT and DYNAMIC_GLOBAL_ACTIONS — plus SEND_EMAIL now derive the caller from that row rather than from userEmail in the request body, satisfying §2 obligations 2 and 4. It fails closed by construction: an absent, unknown, consumed or expired proof leaves the caller empty, the directory matches nobody, and the gate's existing 401 answers, so no second refusal branch was added for the two halves to disagree about. SCAN_INTAKE is deliberately untouched: its body is raw file bytes and it takes the tenant-authenticated principal header, which is a stronger identity than a bearer proof. It is a token in a ledger, not a signed structure, because Power Automate has no HMAC function; fabricating a signature from string concatenation would be worse than a lookup. The ledger is what makes the token mean anything, and revocation is one Consumed flag rather than a key rotation. What remains is application and the obligations this does not touch: §2 obligations 5, 6 and 7 — per-action authorisation beyond the permission each gate already checks, idempotency, and server-side audit of the proof-derived identity — are unchanged. SPLIT 2026-09-24. The OTP package this built was one flow switching on an action, serving both OTP_GENERATE and OTP_VERIFY. The estate does not work that way and the platform owner's mapping settles it: two flows, two trigger URLs, two contract keys. A single flow behind both means revoking the URL that mints codes also revokes the one that verifies them, and the rate limit protecting minting is reached by a caller who only wants to verify. The two packages are built from the one body's own parts rather than by re-typing either case. The end-to-end path is docs/deployment/RUNBOOK.md, which sequences ITEM-64, ITEM-63, G-04 and ITEM-2 as four phases in the only order that avoids rework: the ledger before the installs, because doing it after means rebuilding and reinstalling all eight internal packages; the migration decisions before any export, because they set which flow each package goes into; and ITEM-2 closing on evidence taken during the first install rather than as separate work. PASTED 2026-10-06 (Owner report, 2026-10-06): OTP_VERIFY and the ten verifying packages are in the tenant; the switch is not yet set.

items.title: The upload SHA-256 cannot be computed on this tenant — the digest is recorded, not enforced
items.sourceRegister: OPEN_ITEMS.md item 18
items.description: INT-002 requires the upload to verify size and SHA-256 against the arriving bytes. Size is met: the package compares DeclaredSizeBytes to Content-Length and answers 422 on a mismatch. The digest cannot be. Workflow Definition Language has no hash function and no bitwise operators, so the only route inside Power Automate is an inline-code action, and the operator confirmed on 2026-09-03 that this tenant cannot run one. That is not an unwritten action or a porting job — it is a platform constraint, and no implementation closes it.

evidence.states: the operator's answer, attributed and dated, recorded as an external dependency rather than as a measurement — it is the one fact here not derived from this repository
DeclaredSha256 is declared on Portal Attachments and on Portal Upload Tickets, and the 2026-09-02 dry run reported both present in the tenant — so the declared digest is persisted
digestOf() computes a real SHA-256 through crypto.subtle and declares one per attachment; it returns the empty string where crypto.subtle is absent, and an empty digest is not refused
Verify_Upload_Checksum, typed Javascript — not a Power Automate action type — comparing against an uninterpolated string literal. It has never run and must not be ported
passes: no document claims the digest is verified, and the claim is mutation-tested

items.whyOpen: Accepted 2026-09-03, not closed by work. The requirement stands and cannot be met on this tenant. What is in place instead is disclosed above and is deliberately not described as an integrity control.
dependencies: Confirmation that the environment's licensing permits Execute JavaScript Code.
constraints: Until closed, no document may claim the digest is verified. npm run test:claims enforces this.
risks: A file of the correct declared length whose contents differ from what the submitter intended is stored without objection. The size check still applies and still catches a length mismatch.
A caller who controls the client declares the digest as well as the bytes, so the stored value is only as trustworthy as the caller. It is evidence of accidental corruption, not of tampering.
decisions: The digest is RECORDED, not ENFORCED. A client-computed SHA-256 is stored as DeclaredSha256 and supports out-of-band verification later; nothing verifies it at intake.
The design example is not to be ported under any circumstance. It is typed Javascript, which does not exist, and compares against an uninterpolated literal, so a correct digest would be refused.
requirements: That no document, page or contract describes the upload digest as verified, checked or enforced.
steps: Nothing to execute. If the tenant's Power Automate plan or region later provides an inline-code action, revisit this record: the action must then be written from scratch and demonstrated with two live uploads, one correct and one corrupted.
items.resolutionCriteria: Accepted rather than resolved. The criterion is that the constraint stays recorded and unclaimed: npm run test:claims continues to pass, and the acceptance record remains cited by this item.
items.validation: node tests/standing-claims.test.mjs — the digest-verified claim is absent from every scanned document and fails when mutated in.

items.description: AUTO_SCHEDULED_SWEEP's first live run returned status 400, 'The attempted operation is prohibited because it exceeds the list view threshold', twice — once for Get_Ack_Overdue and once for Get_Due_Breached. Global Tracking Queue held 15,804 items at capture, three times SharePoint's 5,000 threshold, and both queries filtered AND sorted on a date column carrying no index, so neither could be resolved. The threshold applies twice over and both halves had to be answered: the query must be resolvable through an index, AND the clause it resolves must return under 5,000 rows. 'DueDate lt now' on a task list is every task ever due, which no index makes small. The flow now asks for a 30-day window ordered newest-first, which is the code half; the columns still need indexes, which is this item. Three further targets are latent rather than live: DGO_FETCH_ALL sorts both big lists on Modified and DGO_GET_DOCS sorts DGO DIGITAL OPS on it with no filter at all when no reference is supplied — past the threshold SharePoint refuses to SORT on an unindexed column exactly as it refuses to filter on one, so the boot call fails the same way the moment that package is pasted.

items.sourceRegister: root cause of ITEM-45
items.description: The preflight generator and tests/index-targets.test.mjs both extracted filtered columns with the pattern '<Col> eq ', and neither looked at $orderby at all. The scheduled sweep filtered with 'lt' and sorted on the same column, so both detectors saw nothing, the preflight printed READY TO PASTE, and the flow was imported. A check written to catch exactly this class of failure could not see the instance of it that reached production. Both now read eq/ne/lt/le/gt/ge plus startswith and substringof, and both read $orderby. The preflight's mustIndex also stopped being an intersection with a curated list — a column could previously only be reported as needing an index if someone had already written it down, which makes the check incapable of finding anything new. It is now driven by the size of the list, which is the property the threshold actually depends on.

evidence.states: every operator, $orderby, and mustIndex driven by itemsAtCapture over 5,000
the same widening; it found five undeclared columns immediately
regenerated: Global Tracking Queue now names four columns to index, DGO DIGITAL OPS two

items.title: Officers are never told of assignments, approvals, escalations, delegations or reminders
items.description: The assignment cascade requires an assignee and a due date on every assignment and resolves a supporting unit, a supporting assignee and a copy-to list besides. Neither DGO_SINGLE_ASSIGNMENT nor DGO_BULK_ASSIGNMENT carries any mail action, so none of those audiences is written to. pending_review can only be left by a second person's decision and nothing tells that person it is waiting. The acknowledgment module's remind-assignee and FastTrack's notify-owner both report to the operator that a notice was queued; both write only to browser storage, and notify-owner has no action-ownership spec at all, so it runs with no declared backend or audit vocabulary. The FastTrack escalation action writes an escalation record with status Open that reaches nobody, escalate-non-ack is a charter capability with no implementation at all, the orchestrator's set-reminder records a dueAt that nothing reads at that time, and executive-escalate delegates a record to a person who is never told it is theirs. Separately, Deployed - Create Task DOES notify the assignee from the task's AssignedTo field — and DGO_SINGLE_ASSIGNMENT, the package that replaces it, carries no mail action, so pasting it removes the one working assignment notice in the estate.

items.sourceRegister: carried from claude/system-notifications-provisioning-h5h1gy, where it was ITEM-43; renumbered on consolidation 2026-09-05 because ITEM-43 names a different item on the branch it merged into
items.description: CG_SEND_EMAIL, created in the tenant on 2026-09-02 from DGO_SEND_EMAIL, carries triggerAuthenticationType 'All' — anyone holding the signed URL can invoke it. Web - Send Email, the flow it replaces, is one of only five Request triggers in the whole estate set to 'Tenant'. Re-pointing EMAIL at the new flow without changing this takes an internal officer endpoint from tenant-restricted to open-with-URL. It matters more here than on a read endpoint: the flow's authorisation gate resolves the caller from DGO_UserDirectory using the userEmail in the REQUEST BODY, which an anonymous caller supplies. So with an 'All' trigger, anyone with the URL can name any active officer and have the registry mailbox send mail to any address of their choosing — the open relay the 401 gate exists to prevent, defeated one layer below it. The gate is sound for a tenant-authenticated trigger, where the platform has already established who is calling.

items.title: The estate's one sanctioned Tenant crossing is not Tenant in the tenant
items.sourceRegister: raised 2026-09-24 from the first reading in this work taken FROM the tenant rather than from a supplied export; in no register before 1.3.0
items.description: DECISIONS.md D6 names IP_SCAN_INTAKE as the single sanctioned crossing into the internal platform and requires triggerAuthenticationType = Tenant. The repository's export of that flow — workflow 5504d7f9-cc96-470c-be79-217582faf415, exported 2026-09-04 — says Tenant, and npm run triggerauth has reported green on it ever since. A live read of the same flow id through the Flow Management API on 2026-09-18 says All. The flow was last modified 2026-09-13, is in state Started, and its body is otherwise unchanged: it still derives its actor from coalesce(triggerOutputs()?['headers']?['x-ms-client-principal-name'], ...), byte-for-byte the same expression the recorded export carries and the same one tests/auth-posture.test.mjs asserts. That expression is the whole reason this endpoint is the sanctioned one: it is the ONLY endpoint in the estate whose actor comes from a platform-supplied principal instead of request.body.userEmail. A Tenant trigger is what makes the platform supply it. With All set, it does not. TWO READINGS FOLLOW AND THIS REPOSITORY CANNOT DISTINGUISH THEM. If Power Automate strips inbound x-ms-client-principal-* headers on an unauthenticated trigger, the coalesce falls to '', the DGO_UserDirectory lookup finds nobody, and every deposit is refused — a functional outage that would look like a data problem. If it does not strip them, the header is caller-supplied and the actor on the estate's only authenticated crossing is whatever the caller types. One is a break, the other is an impersonation path; which it is is a question about the platform's header handling, not about this code, and it is not answerable from here. Either way the guard is measuring the wrong artefact: npm run triggerauth reads docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/contracts/deployed, so its green tick describes the 2026-09-04 export, not what is running. All twenty flows in that live reading carry All. Not one carries Tenant. The estate has no tenant-authenticated crossing at present. A second flow shows the same movement earlier and is NOT drift against the current record: badb65d8-f472-407e-8975-c29d77b855d7 was Tenant with no method on 2026-08-19 as Portal_Status_Enquiry and All/POST by 2026-09-03 as CG_Status_Check_Endpoint — both exports are in this repository, so that change is recorded and only this one is not. The repository holds no decision widening SCAN_INTAKE, and the rebuild argues against one: IP_SCAN_INTAKE_Endpoint_v2.1, packaged 2026-09-13 — the same day the live flow was modified — carries Tenant/PUT. Whoever built the successor kept the posture. Recording that this was deliberate, if it was, closes this item as ACCEPTED and retires D6's claim; nothing here assumes it was not. RESOLVED 2026-09-24. A fresh export of the same flow id — not a report that the change was made — reads triggerAuthenticationType Tenant, method PUT, state Started, lastModifiedTime 2026-09-24T04:55:02Z. The crossing is tenant-authenticated again and npm run triggerauth is once more measuring what is deployed. The header-handling question in step 5 was not answered and did not need to be: it decided which of the two risks had been live, and with the setting restored neither is. It is worth asking once, out of band, so the next person to widen a trigger knows what it costs.

items.whyOpen: Closed 2026-09-24 on a fresh export of the same flow id reading Tenant, not on a report that the setting was changed. The flow was modified at 04:55:02Z that day and is Started. It was raised because the repository's guard was green on a 2026-09-04 export while the tenant read All; that gap is gone, and npm run triggerauth now measures what is deployed.
dependencies: Tenant administrator access to the flow's trigger settings.
constraints: Do NOT import IP_SCAN_INTAKE_Endpoint_v2.1_NOTIFICATIONS_REPORTS_20260913.zip to fix this. It carries Tenant, but its flow id is 12b6e690-a065-468d-b470-fcfba015f1f8 — a different flow that no wired endpoint resolves to. Importing it stands up a second flow or overwrites a live one with a definition that was never in service. See ITEM-60.

If it does not: the actor on the estate's only authenticated crossing is caller-supplied, and the one endpoint that does not trust request.body.userEmail effectively does.
Until it is settled, npm run triggerauth reports green on a posture that is not deployed — the most expensive kind of false green this estate has, because it is the control guarding the crossing.
decisions: 2026-09-24: raised. Not treated as a reading error first: the same flow id was read from two sources a fortnight apart, the package rebuilt on the modification date kept Tenant, and the repository holds no decision to widen it.

5. Separately, and whatever step 2 finds: confirm against the platform whether an All trigger strips inbound x-ms-client-principal-* headers. That answer decides which of the two risks above was live, and it is worth knowing even once the setting is back.

items.title: Six of the twenty supplied export packages are not exports of any deployed flow, and three of those answer every verb
items.sourceRegister: raised 2026-09-24 on joining docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/artifacts/matched-flow-packages/ to the tenant reading; in no register before 1.3.0
items.description: Twenty Power Automate export packages were supplied and committed under docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/artifacts/matched-flow-packages/2026-09-24/. Fourteen are exports of flows a wired endpoint actually resolves to, and where the tenant reading carries the same flow all thirteen agree with it on trigger posture. Six are not: IP_Create_Email_Assignment_Endpoint (2fbb5485), IP_Dynamic_Global_Actions_Endpoint (31c0aaf0), IP_FETCH_ALL__EXTENDED_ENDPOINT (ce2cbed8), IP_Get_Docs_Endpoint (28f6e62a), IP_SCAN_INTAKE_Endpoint_v2.1 (12b6e690) and the related alternative IP_Bulk_Assignment_Endpoint (f96399c6). Each is a real export of a real flow; none is the flow its name will be taken for. This matters because the obvious thing to do with a package is import it. Importing one of these does not update the endpoint its name suggests — it stands up a different flow, or overwrites a live one with a definition that was never in service. Three of the six declare no HTTP method, so their triggers answer every verb: IP_Dynamic_Global_Actions_Endpoint, IP_Get_Docs_Endpoint and IP_Bulk_Assignment_Endpoint. The flow actually wired behind DYNAMIC_ACTIONS and SUBSIDIARY_ACTIONS is 08da1783, which answers POST only and IS supplied, as IP_Subsidiary_Actions_Endpoint_20260905193834.zip. Importing the Dynamic_Global_Actions package over it would widen a POST-only trigger to every verb — a regression dressed as an update. The join is on the dashed flow id because it is the only identifier all three readings carry. GOV-06 is measured here rather than restated: none of the twenty packages carries a workflow id that any wired endpoint addresses. They do contain 32-hex tokens — environment and connection ids — and every package's fullResourceId is populated, but it restates the dashed flow id in resource form and resolves nothing. The archive's own manifests/contract_to_package_mapping.csv declares five contract keys it does not cover — AI_CHAT, AI_DOC_ANALYSIS, AI_EMAIL_ANALYSIS, BULK_ASSIGNMENT and BULK_ASSIGNMENT_DIRECT — as SOURCE_COLLECTION_NOT_ATTACHED, expected from OTH__FULL_EMBEDDED_CONTENTS.json, which was not supplied. It declares them rather than substituting something else, which is the right behaviour and is recorded here as such. Nothing in this item says the six are wrong. Whether one of them is an intended successor is a decision for whoever built it; this records only that no wired endpoint resolves to it, so it must not be imported as though it did. CORRECTED 2026-09-24, on the operator's account of where those packages went. This item read the archive's SOURCE_COLLECTION_NOT_ATTACHED rows as five contract keys with no package anywhere. That is true of the archive and false of the repository. docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/exports/ already holds AI_Document_Processing_20260911185206.zip and BULKOPSDATARETRIEVALHTTP_20260911185143.zip — the two the archive's mapping named as expected from OTH__FULL_EMBEDDED_CONTENTS.json — together with IP_Bulk_Assign_Endpoint_20260911185130.zip, which the tenant registry does resolve to the wired BULK_ASSIGNMENT_DIRECT workflow. They were imported into that directory earlier, before the matched-package archive was assembled, so the archive's declaration describes what it does not carry, not what is missing. What IS still missing is narrower and is not a package: the tenant registry of 2026-09-18 returns powerAutomateFlowId null for the AI workflow 3f018fea1031490fb73dff6a8d6341f2 and for the bulk workflow a705e453f922457c95ca19f32731e4d7, both recorded as NOT_EVIDENCED. So the AI and BULKOPS packages cannot be joined to a wired endpoint from the tenant side, and the provenance record leaves them unresolved rather than guessing. That is a gap in the JOIN, not in the corpus, and it is GOV-06 again rather than a missing artefact. RESOLVED 2026-09-24 by the platform owner's mapping. This item asked one question — what are the six packages that are exports of flows no wired endpoint resolves to — and the mapping answers it for all six at once: every one of them is the INTENDED flow for a contract key. IP_FETCH_ALL__EXTENDED_ENDPOINT is FETCH_ALL, IP_Get_Docs_Endpoint is GET_DOCS, IP_Bulk_Assignment_Endpoint is BULK_ASSIGNMENT, IP_Dynamic_Global_Actions_Endpoint is DYNAMIC_GLOBAL_ACTIONS, IP_SCAN_INTAKE_Endpoint_v2.1 is SCAN_INTAKE and IP_Create_Email_Assignment_Endpoint is EMAIL_RELATED_TASK. They were never orphans. They are successors, and this repository had no source that could say so. The three import hazards this item recorded are unchanged in substance and change in meaning: importing one of those packages over the flow its name suggests is still wrong, but because it is a MIGRATION requiring the endpoint to be repointed, not because the package is a stray. ITEM-63 carries the four migrations. The five contract keys this item recorded as uncovered are also answered: AI_CHAT, AI_DOC_ANALYSIS and AI_EMAIL_ANALYSIS are all AI_Document_Processing (fefa43c6-fb9d-4337-8b65-7fd19fa09b6d), BULK_ASSIGNMENT is f96399c6 and BULK_ASSIGNMENT_DIRECT is 122bb363. Nothing further is needed from OTH__FULL_EMBEDDED_CONTENTS.json for the join.

items.title: FETCH_ALL computes the refusal, discards it, and serves the estate to anyone
items.sourceRegister: raised 2026-09-24 from a production run record supplied by the operator; in no register before 1.4.0
items.description: The flow behind the wired FETCH_ALL endpoint — IP_FETCH_ALL_BOOTSTRAP, b79e6707-df4d-4ae7-8a65-738aa45e9a73, workflow aa662769f13a4666bfadf3039cd8d247 — reads the caller from the request body, looks that address up in DGO_UserDirectory, reads the role off the row, reads what the role may do, and computes whether the caller is permitted. It then ignores the answer. Compose_FetchAll_Permitted, the value Condition_FetchAll_Authorised branches on, is the literal true. The real expression sits in Compose_FetchAll_Permitted_actual__permission_condition_expression, runs immediately before the decision in the same sequence, and is read by nothing. The condition's else branch contains no actions, so there is no refusal path even structurally. This is not a reading of the code alone. Run 08584115564651739687523527063CU26, 2026-09-22T04:13:41Z, recorded both values in the flow's own telemetry: the caller resolved to the empty string, the role to the empty string, the directory matched zero rows, the real expression evaluated to FALSE, and the value the gate read was TRUE. The flow returned HTTP 200 with 500 documents, 500 tasks, a DGO_UserDirectory record carrying FullName, Email, Role, Persona and AccessScope, 45 categories, 50 departments and 3 comments — 6.1 MB — to a caller that supplied no identity at all. The response carried Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * against a request whose Origin header was null, so no browser-side origin restriction applied either. The trigger is triggerAuthenticationType All, so no sign-in was required to reach it. The estate has a build that DOES enforce. IP_FETCH_ALL__EXTENDED_ENDPOINTFlow_20260911185117.zip carries the real expression in Compose_FetchAll_Permitted itself and has no parked copy. Six days later IP_FETCH_ALL_BOOTSTRAP_20260917225904.zip carries the constant. Both packages have been committed in docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/exports/ since before this item was raised, and the tenant reading of 2026-09-18 resolves the wired FETCH_ALL workflow to the BOOTSTRAP flow. The enforcing build is not the deployed one. Every control in this repository was green through this. npm run triggerauth reads trigger posture and stops at the trigger. The seam tests read request and response shapes. Nothing read a flow's own decision logic, which is why a gate wired to a constant was indistinguishable here from a gate that works. npm run authgates now reads exactly that, across deployed contracts, flow exports and the packages inside committed archives, and finds one match in the whole estate — this one. Read against G-04 this sharpens rather than softens it: the enforcement G-04 says is absent was BUILT, in this flow, and then disconnected. RESOLVED 2026-09-24, and fixed better than this item proposed. The proposal was to move the real expression into Compose_FetchAll_Permitted. What was done instead leaves that Compose at true and compares it against the real expression in the condition — equals(true, <check>) — which is the same decision, and removes the parked action entirely. The else branch, which this item noted held no actions at all, now discriminates two cases the proposal collapsed into one: a caller in the directory but lacking the permission gets 403; a caller in no directory row gets 401. Run 08584113850424042017125920880CU10, 2026-09-24T03:50:43Z, proves it on the input that exposed it. The same caller — empty, matching zero directory rows — that received 6.1 MB on 2026-09-22 received 401 UNAUTHENTICATED, 'The caller is not in DGO_UserDirectory, or is not active', and a 1,413-character response. The superseded package is deliberately still in docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/exports/ and npm run authgates deliberately still flags it: it is the artefact of the defect, and ITEM-60 establishes that packages get imported on the strength of their file name. Anyone importing IP_FETCH_ALL_BOOTSTRAP_20260917225904.zip re-opens this. The fixed export sits beside it as IP_FETCH_ALL_BOOTSTRAP_20260924035751.zip. The audit itself was corrected in the same commit. Its first version tested the SHAPE of a decision — any constant Compose a Condition branched on — and would have reported this correctly fixed flow as a bypass, because the constant is still there. It now tests INVARIANCE: a decision is a bypass only when substituting the constant leaves nothing that can vary. A control that fails on the fix teaches people to ignore it. What this does NOT close is the reason the caller was empty and could have been anyone: Compose_FetchAll_Caller still reads userEmail from the request body. A caller who names an active directory user is now authorised as that user. That is G-04, unchanged, and it is now the whole of the problem rather than part of it. CORRECTED 2026-09-24 on the operator's account: the run that demonstrated this was their own test, made at this repository's request for a run record. That changes nothing about the defect — the gate was pinned to a constant, the refusal was computed and discarded, and the fix is proven — and it removes the disclosure reading built on top of it. ITEM-62, which asked whether the run was notifiable, is withdrawn.

items.whyOpen: Closed 2026-09-24. The disclosure question in step 5 is NOT closed by this and is carried by the agency.
dependencies: Tenant edit access to the flow.
constraints: Do not fix this by importing IP_FETCH_ALL__EXTENDED_ENDPOINTFlow_20260911185117.zip over it. That package is flow ce2cbed8-d180-4160-a0c7-f552101bc412, which no wired endpoint resolves to — see ITEM-60. Read its Compose_FetchAll_Permitted, and put that expression into the deployed flow.

Restoring the expression does not by itself authenticate the caller: Compose_FetchAll_Caller still reads userEmail from the REQUEST BODY, which anyone can set. That is G-04 and is not closed by this item.
risks: Any party who can reach the endpoint URL can read the estate: documents, tasks, directory records with names and email addresses, and the organisational structure. The trigger requires no sign-in.
It is already known to have happened once, on 2026-09-22, and the flow has been in this state since 2026-09-17 at the latest.
Personal data left the tenant to an unidentified caller. Whether that is notifiable is a question for the agency, not for this repository, and it should be asked rather than assumed.
The parked expression makes this look deliberate and temporary — the kind of change made to unblock a demo. Nothing recorded it, and nothing would have surfaced it.
decisions: 2026-09-24: raised on the operator's own run record. Not inferred from the definition alone: the flow's telemetry carries the computed false and the read true in the same run.
2026-09-24: an earlier reading in this work that reported FETCH_ALL enforcing correctly is superseded here. It described the EXTENDED build, which enforces and is not deployed.
requirements: Compose_FetchAll_Permitted in the deployed flow reads the real permission expression.
A run record showing an unpermitted caller refused.
A decision from the agency on whether the 2026-09-22 disclosure is notifiable.
steps: 1. Open the flow at b79e6707-df4d-4ae7-8a65-738aa45e9a73. Set Compose_FetchAll_Permitted's input to the expression currently sitting in Compose_FetchAll_Permitted_actual__permission_condition_expression, and delete the parked action so there is one decision.

2. Give Condition_FetchAll_Authorised an else branch that sets 403 and a refusal body. Today it has none, so even a correct expression would fall through to the finalize scope with whatever varStatusCode holds.
3. Call the endpoint with an address in no directory row and keep the run record. It must refuse.

4. Export the flow and replace docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/exports/IP_FETCH_ALL_BOOTSTRAP_20260917225904.zip, then run npm run authgates and settle KNOWN in scripts/audit-authorisation-gates.mjs in the same commit.
5. Ask the agency whether 2026-09-22 requires notification. Give them the run record, not a summary of it.
6. Separately: every other endpoint takes its caller from the request body too. That is G-04 and is the larger problem this one sits inside.
items.owner: Platform technical owner for the flow; the agency for the disclosure question
items.resolutionCriteria: npm run authgates finds no decision pinned to a constant, a dated run record shows an unpermitted caller refused with 403, and the agency has recorded its position on the 2026-09-22 disclosure. Met on the first two: npm run authgates finds no live decision pinned to a constant, and run 08584113850424042017125920880CU10 shows an unpermitted caller refused with 401. The third criterion — an agency position on the 2026-09-22 run — is void: that run was an operator test, not a disclosure, and ITEM-62 is withdrawn.
items.validation: npm run authgates reads every flow definition in the repository — including packages nested two archives deep, which is where this one was — and fails on a new constant-pinned decision. One injected mutation confirmed it.

items.title: Raised in error: the 2026-09-22 FETCH_ALL run was an operator test, not a disclosure
items.sourceRegister: split from ITEM-61 on 2026-09-24 when the defect was fixed and the question was not
items.description: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-24, the day it was raised. This item asked whether the FETCH_ALL run of 2026-09-22 required data-protection notification. It should never have been raised. That run was performed by the operator, on this repository's own request for a run record. An unauthenticated call from an Android browser, arriving at the moment a run record was asked for, is a test. This repository read it as a caller of unknown provenance, wrote 'who sent it is not recorded' into the evidence, and then built a notifiable-disclosure question on that ambiguity — complete with a clock said to run from awareness. The ambiguity was manufactured here, from the operator's own output. No data left the tenant. It went to the person who runs the platform, from their own device, while producing evidence this repository had asked for. What the run does establish is unaffected and is carried by ITEM-61, which is closed: the deployed flow would have served the estate to a caller with no identity, the refusal was computed and discarded, and that is fixed and proven fixed. A real defect demonstrated by a test is still a real defect. It is not an incident.

evidence.states: the run and who performed it, and that the defect it demonstrates is real while the run itself is a test.
the same call refused with 401 two days later. The defect is closed; ITEM-61 carries it.

items.whyOpen: Closed 2026-09-24 as raised in error. The run was a test performed by the operator at this repository's request; treating its output as a possible external disclosure was an escalation of the operator's own evidence, not a finding.

items.title: Four contract keys are wired to a different flow from the one intended
items.sourceRegister: split from ITEM-60 on 2026-09-24 when the mapping resolved what the six packages were
items.description: The platform owner's mapping names the flow each contract key should be served by. For nineteen of twenty-three, that is the flow the endpoint is already wired to. For four it is not, and the difference is not an error in either source: the mapping states the intent and the register states what is answering traffic today. FETCH_ALL: intended IP_FETCH_ALL__EXTENDED_ENDPOINT (ce2cbed8-d180-4160-a0c7-f552101bc412), wired b79e6707-df4d-4ae7-8a65-738aa45e9a73, be1f89bd-d7ea-4a15-87c9-2ce6fd4d0eaa; BULK_ASSIGNMENT_DIRECT: intended Deployed Bulk Task Assignment_Create Task (122bb363-ddea-40c7-8578-d0d613a17bf7), wired 0d1e8df5-30b3-4069-8903-665b87c197eb; DYNAMIC_GLOBAL_ACTIONS: intended IP_Dynamic_Global_Actions_Endpoint (31c0aaf0-ddbb-478c-9a98-bc013265c4c7), wired 08da1783-927f-4662-a429-45e1249a989f; SCAN_INTAKE: intended IP_SCAN_INTAKE_Endpoint_v2.1 (12b6e690-a065-468d-b470-fcfba015f1f8), wired 5504d7f9-cc96-470c-be79-217582faf415. The trigger URL belongs to the WIRED flow. So installing a package into the intended flow does not move the endpoint — it leaves a correct, updated flow sitting behind no URL while the endpoint goes on reaching the old one. Each of the four needs a decision before anything is installed: repoint the endpoint to the intended flow after installing, or install into the wired flow and treat the mapping as a later cutover. FETCH_ALL is the one to look at first. The wired flow, IP_FETCH_ALL_BOOTSTRAP, is the one that served the estate to an unauthenticated caller on 2026-09-22 (ITEM-61, closed). The intended flow, IP_FETCH_ALL__EXTENDED_ENDPOINT, is a different build whose authorisation decision this repository has read and which carries the real permission expression rather than a constant. Whether the estate should migrate to it or keep the repaired incumbent is a decision, and it is not ITEM-61 reopening: that item closed on the incumbent being fixed and proven fixed. EMAIL added 2026-09-24 and CONFIRMED, not migrating. Two packages were supplied for it and compared field by field: identical across all 70 actions and both connector maps, differing only in two metadata timestamps eight minutes apart and the display name. IP_SEND_EMAIL (df59a69f-92ca-4554-ae68-6b464aa73ef7) is adopted because it is what the key is wired to; IP_DGO_SEND_EXTERNAL_CORRESPONDENCE (faceec58-fa79-4de5-87b6-6376faff8a1a) is the earlier save, is wired to nothing, and is recorded as a duplicate rather than adopted alongside it — which would have created the very hazard ITEM-60 was raised about. The migration count is unchanged at four. The end-to-end path is docs/deployment/RUNBOOK.md, which sequences ITEM-64, ITEM-63, G-04 and ITEM-2 as four phases in the only order that avoids rework: the ledger before the installs, because doing it after means rebuilding and reinstalling all eight internal packages; the migration decisions before any export, because they set which flow each package goes into; and ITEM-2 closing on evidence taken during the first install rather than as separate work.

dependencies: Tenant access to repoint an endpoint or to install into a flow.
constraints: Do not install a package into an intended flow and assume the endpoint follows. It does not: the trigger URL belongs to the wired flow.
risks: A package installed into the intended flow with the endpoint left pointing at the old one is the worst outcome available: the work is done, the estate is unchanged, and everything reports success.
decisions: 2026-09-24: recorded as four separate decisions rather than one migration. They share a shape and nothing else — SCAN_INTAKE's incumbent was just restored to Tenant, FETCH_ALL's was just repaired, and the other two are untouched.

2026-10-05 (owner, by the identification Phase 3 and 4 pastes; recorded in registers/flow-adoption.json): FETCH_ALL — install into the wired flow b79e6707 (the map's ce2cbed8 is retired); DYNAMIC_GLOBAL_ACTIONS — 31c0aaf0, which the 2026-09-27 live read shows the key on; SCAN_INTAKE — the wired flow 5504d7f9 (the map's 12b6e690 is retired); BULK_ASSIGNMENT_DIRECT — retired with its flows, called by nothing in Folio.
requirements: For each of the four: repoint, or defer, recorded.
steps: 1. Read docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/reference/contract-key-flow-reconciliation.json, the four rows with verdict MIGRATION.
2. For each, decide: install into the intended flow and repoint the endpoint, or install into the wired flow and keep the mapping as a target.
3. Record the decision. A migration nobody decided against is one that will be half-done.
4. FETCH_ALL first, because its incumbent and its intended flow differ in their authorisation logic and ITEM-61 is only closed against the incumbent.

items.title: The internal proof ledger is decided separate and is not yet provisioned
items.sourceRegister: raised 2026-09-24 on the platform owner's instruction that the two surfaces use separate flows
items.description: The flows are separate and always were: the Correspondence Gateway portal runs CG_* / Portal_* flows and the internal platform runs IP_* / DGO_* flows, with no flow serving both. What they now share is the proof LEDGER. When internal proof verification was built on 2026-09-24 it was pointed at the list the portal already used, on the argument that one ledger means a proof means the same thing on both surfaces. That argument was made here and should have been put to the platform owner instead. The two are separated today by a single field. The portal mints Purpose 'portal-verification' and reads back on that value; the internal flows mint 'internal-session' and read back on that value. Every one of the eleven flows that touches the ledger filters on its own Purpose, so a portal proof cannot authorise an internal call and vice versa. The separation holds — it is just one WHERE clause wide. A separate list would make the boundary structural rather than conditional: a filter that is edited, generated wrongly, or omitted in a flow built later cannot cross a boundary that does not exist. It costs one provisioned list and the columns the portal's already has. This is not implemented, deliberately. The list GUID would have to be real — tests/designer-paste-schema.test.mjs refuses a package carrying a REPLACE_WITH placeholder, correctly — so the list must exist in the tenant before the builder can name it. Inventing a GUID to make the build pass would put an unresolvable reference into every internal package. DECIDED 2026-09-24: separate. The platform owner reversed the argument this repository made for sharing, and the reversal is right — a shared list is separated by a WHERE clause, and a clause can be edited, generated wrongly, or omitted in a flow written later, where a separate list gives a boundary there is nothing to cross. It is implemented as far as it can be without tenant access. docs/reference/internal-proof-ledger.json carries the decision, the list to provision — DGO_SessionProofs on the governance site, where DGO_UserDirectory and DGO_RoleCatalogue already are, with the six columns a verifier reads back and Title indexed because every authenticated call in the estate does one lookup on it — and a null listId. scripts/build-internal-designer-paste.mjs reads that file and will use the list the moment the GUID is set; until then it falls back to the portal's ledger with the Purpose filter, visibly and by declaration rather than silently. A GUID cannot be invented: a package naming a list that does not exist fails at install rather than at build, and the paste-schema gate correctly refuses a placeholder. The interim is now gated rather than assumed. npm run test:proofidentity asserts, on the packages themselves, that every flow READING the shared ledger filters on Purpose and every flow WRITING to it stamps Purpose — two different obligations that an earlier draft of the check conflated, failing the minter for not reading what it writes. Once listId is set the same check inverts: naming the portal ledger becomes a regression rather than a fallback. Both directions were mutation-tested. The end-to-end path is docs/deployment/RUNBOOK.md, which sequences ITEM-64, ITEM-63, G-04 and ITEM-2 as four phases in the only order that avoids rework: the ledger before the installs, because doing it after means rebuilding and reinstalling all eight internal packages; the migration decisions before any export, because they set which flow each package goes into; and ITEM-2 closing on evidence taken during the first install rather than as separate work. 2026-10-07: the owner created DGO_SessionProofs (list 444102d6-2c29-45cf-8b59-52774d7c4dd4); docs/reference/internal-proof-ledger.json records it and release 2 names it in the mint and every verifying package. Writing OTP_VERIFY was refused: "The API operation does not contain a definition for parameter item/Email", so the list lacks at least the Email column.

the internal mint, writing Purpose 'internal-session' into the same list.
that every internal flow's proof lookup filters on Purpose and on Consumed — the assertions that make the current separation checkable rather than assumed.
the decision, the list to provision with its six columns and the index Title needs, the one blocking value, and what holds the boundary until it is supplied.
the interim boundary enforced on the packages: readers filter on Purpose, the minter stamps it. It inverts to require the provisioned list once listId is set.
this item's place in the four-phase cutover, the steps it contributes, and what closes it.
OTP_VERIFY refused: item/Email is not a column of the list
SINGLE_ASSIGNMENT, BULK_ASSIGNMENT, FETCH_ALL now read the new list
fields before (Title only); five columns created with the specified internal names, required, DateTime as date and time, Consumed default 0; Title indexed and required; read-back of every field
REFERENCE_DATA, GET_DOCS, FETCH_EMAIL_ATTACHMENTS, EMAIL and AI_DOC_ANALYSIS written with release 3 and read back (proof reads on DGO_SessionProofs)

items.whyOpen: Closed 2026-10-07: DGO_SessionProofs columns created and read back, and all six dependent flows written with release 3 and read back (five at 20:26, OTP_VERIFY at 20:44 once the Flow service refreshed its list schema). The internal proof ledger is now separate from the portal's.
dependencies: A provisioned SharePoint list for internal session proofs, with the columns the portal's ledger carries: Title, Email, Purpose, ExpiresAtUtc, CreatedAtUtc, Consumed.
constraints: Do not name a list GUID in a package before the list exists. The paste-schema gate refuses placeholders, and a package carrying an unresolvable list id fails at install rather than at build.
risks: The boundary is one WHERE clause. A flow built later that omits the Purpose filter reads across it, and nothing outside npm run test:proofidentity would notice.
Retaining the shared ledger is defensible. Recording that it was never decided is not.
decisions: 2026-09-24: raised rather than implemented. The argument for sharing was made in this repository without the platform owner being asked, and the instruction of the same day points the other way.
2026-10-06: the decision is carried by scripts/build-identification-phase4.mjs, which reads listId; the DGO_* generator that read it is retired.
requirements: A decision: separate list, or shared ledger with the Purpose filter as the accepted boundary.
If separate: the list provisioned, then the internal builder repointed and every internal package rebuilt.
steps: 1. In DGO_SessionProofs add the columns Email (Single line of text), Purpose (Single line of text), ExpiresAtUtc (Date and time, include time), CreatedAtUtc (Date and time, include time), Consumed (Yes/No); index Title.
2. npm run flows:update -- apply --only OTP_VERIFY,REFERENCE_DATA,GET_DOCS,FETCH_EMAIL_ATTACHMENTS,EMAIL__IP_SEND_EMAIL,AI_DOC_ANALYSIS__AI_Document_Processing__fefa43c6.
3. Live read: every package carries release 3.
items.owner: operator (the list); the decision is settled
items.resolutionCriteria: listId set to a provisioned list, the internal packages rebuilt against it, and npm run test:proofidentity passing its inverted assertion — no internal package naming the portal ledger.
items.validation: npm run test:proofidentity asserts the Purpose and Consumed filters on every internal proof lookup, so the boundary as it stands is enforced whichever way the decision goes.

items.title: Live endpoint wiring differs from the owner's map for nine keys, and SUBSIDIARY_ACTIONS has no flow that implements it
items.sourceRegister: raised 2026-09-27 from a live read of every wired workflow id (estate-apply.cli.mjs values, flow-owner account, 693 of 693 flows read)
items.description: The live read records, for each endpoint key, the flow that answers the workflow id the platform is built with. Of the 25 keys, 15 are on the flow contract-key-flow-map.json names and 9 are not: FETCH_ALL (b79e6707), SINGLE_ASSIGNMENT (3caf9458), BULK_ASSIGNMENT (5aab9e61), BULK_ASSIGNMENT_DIRECT (0d1e8df5), EMAIL_RELATED_TASK (3f2f649b), OTP_GENERATE (4dbe6dde, shared with OTP_VERIFY), SUBSIDIARY_ACTIONS (31c0aaf0, shared with DYNAMIC_ACTIONS), SCAN_INTAKE (5504d7f9) and the portal's VERIFY (ba47f79b). FETCH_ACTIVITIES has no row in the owner's map. Three contradict the 2026-09-18 tenant reading the reconciliation is built from: DYNAMIC_ACTIONS and SUBSIDIARY_ACTIONS answer on 31c0aaf0 (IP_Dynamic_Global_Actions_Endpoint), not 08da1783; EMAIL_RELATED_TASK answers on 3f2f649b, not 2fbb5485. The blocking consequence: SUBSIDIARY_ACTIONS, and FETCH_ACTIVITIES with it, is meant to move to IP_Subsidiary_Actions_Endpoint (08da1783), but that flow lacks LIST-ACTIVITIES live, and the export held of it (docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/exports/IP_Subsidiary_Actions_Endpoint_20260905193834.zip) implements none of the 18 routes config/endpoints.config.js declares. No package in this repository implements them. Until one does, DYNAMIC_ACTIONS/SUBSIDIARY_ACTIONS and FETCH_ACTIVITIES/GET_DOCS stay on shared flows, npm run package refuses the internal-platform package for those two pairs, and DGO_DYNAMIC_GLOBAL_ACTIONS and DGO_GET_DOCS cannot be installed without taking the other key down. SCAN_INTAKE is MISSING from the values by design: its trigger is Tenant (ITEM-59), so it has no signed address. RESOLVED 2026-10-07: every endpoint trigger URL read through the Flow API (every key signed except SCAN_INTAKE, whose trigger requires a Microsoft sign-in by design); no workflow collision; both packages built from the values and verified against their manifests. The register wired EMAIL_RELATED_TASK to a942d230, the workflow of the retired and switched-off copy 2fbb5485; corrected to the adopted flow ab1a3555 (workflow 8fbf2896fceb4567afe9ebf47628c3a1, cu/11).

items.title: Most mail sends write no delivery receipt, and nothing proves a message arrived
items.description: Only a minority of the estate's mail actions write a row to the Portal Outbox Receipts ledger; for the rest the only evidence of a send is flow run history, which expires. Every notification status in the matrix is derived from definitions and code, and a correctly addressed send in a definition is not evidence that anything arrived. The tenant evidence gate exists to close this and its delivery evidence is not yet captured. PACKAGED 2026-10-06 for every flow with an identification package: the Phase 3 and Phase 4 builders add, after each mail send, a Portal Outbox Receipts row (message type, the send's own recipient, the run as reference, sent or failed, the error on failure; never the body) and an outcome step that fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope still fails and the flow's catch path still fires (scripts/lib/identification-flow-edit.mjs outboxReceipts). That covers the eight portal packages and the internal packages' sends (SUBMISSION, UPLOAD, STATUS, SUPPORT, WRITEBACK, the status notifier, the daily sweep, SCAN_INTAKE, FETCH_ALL, GET_DOCS, REFERENCE_DATA, DYNAMIC_ACTIONS, SINGLE and BULK assignment, the email-to-task flow, OTP). IP_SEND_EMAIL and the scheduled sweep already wrote receipts. Not covered, because no package carries them: CG_Portal_Verification_Endpoint (ba47f79b), CG_Portal_Verification_Confirmation_Endpoint (f96e3448), ECM_DOCS_INTAKE (df7ddff1) and the eight GOV registry flows. 2026-10-06 (Owner report, 2026-10-06): the eleven Phase 4 packages are pasted, so their sends write receipts in the tenant; the Phase 3 packages carrying the portal sends' receipts are not yet re-pasted. 2026-10-06: CG_Portal_Verification_Endpoint (ba47f79b) and CG_Portal_Verification_Confirmation_Endpoint (f96e3448) are now carried by identification Phase 3 packages (from their conformance packages) so their sends write receipts too; npm run test:idphase3 and test:idphase4 assert that every send in every package has a receipt and an outcome step. Left without a package: ECM_DOCS_INTAKE (one telemetry mail, an ITEM-52 surplus send) and the eight GOV registry flows (governance reports and alerts).

items.title: A task raised from an e-mail never reaches Folio, and its follow-up write lands on another task
items.description: The flow behind EMAIL_RELATED_TASK has four defects. (1) It read Email.id and NewActivityTask.* at the top level of the request, while Folio sends {action, payload:{email, title, assignedTo, …}} (core/data-client.js, core/assignment-payload.js buildEmailTaskPayload), so Folio's requests carried no e-mail id and were refused at validation. (2) It created the task in DEV_OPS_Global_Tracking_Queue (22c4e38d), a test list (owner direction, 2026-10-05: tasks are created in Global Tracking Queue), which Folio does not read, then patched Global Tracking Queue (ee82725a) at the DEV_OPS item's ID, writing Reference_ID, TaskType, TaskTypeChoice and GTQGrouping onto whichever unrelated task holds that ID. (3) DueDate called type(), which is not a workflow expression function, and was null for any text date. (4) StartDate, the acknowledgement due date and the task description used formatDateTime() and trim() in the untaken branch of if(), which the service evaluates, so a request without those fields failed. Three tenant flows hold this definition, identical apart from designer metadata: IP_Create_Email_Assignment (3f2f649b, the flow the 2026-09-27 live read found Folio's URL answering on, ITEM-65), IP_Create_Email_Assignment_Endpoint (2fbb5485) and IP_Create__Task__for_received_Email_Endpoint (ab1a3555). The adoption ledger (registers/flow-adoption.json, 2026-10-05) adopts ab1a3555, the copy the owner supplied, and retires 3f2f649b and 2fbb5485. The Phase 4 package fixes all four and adds the identification fields (TASK-YYYY-NNNNN, Entity Key, the e-mail's record as parent when it is registered). APPLIED 2026-10-06 (Owner report, 2026-10-06): the package is pasted and the two retired copies are off.

items.title: The last five internal endpoint flows carry G-04 in packages not yet pasted
items.description: The DGO_* replacement packages designed G-04 (the caller from the sign-in proof) and directory fixes for every internal endpoint. They are retired with the flows they replaced; the identification packages carry G-04 for FETCH_ALL, SINGLE_ASSIGNMENT, BULK_ASSIGNMENT, DYNAMIC_ACTIONS (and SUBSIDIARY_ACTIONS) and EMAIL_RELATED_TASK, mint the proof in IP_OTP_VERIFY, and port the directory fixes into FETCH_ALL. Not yet carried on the adopted flows: G-04 for REFERENCE_DATA (IP_Reference_Data_Endpoint), GET_DOCS and FETCH_ACTIVITIES (IP_Get_Docs_Endpoint), FETCH_EMAIL_ATTACHMENTS, EMAIL (IP_SEND_EMAIL) and the three AI keys (AI_Document_Processing); and in IP_Reference_Data_Endpoint, the directory read in pages past 500 rows, Role/Persona/Status served as text, Departments and Categories read by their internal field names, and the full directory served only to a holder of user:view. The retired designs are held at the commit registers/flow-retirement.json names. BUILT 2026-10-06. scripts/build-identification-phase4.mjs now builds a package for each: REFERENCE_DATA__IP_Reference_Data_Endpoint__9a4dea8e, GET_DOCS__IP_Get_Docs_Endpoint__28f6e62a, FETCH_EMAIL_ATTACHMENTS__IP_Retrieve_Email_Attachment_Endpoint__5bc87cf3, EMAIL__IP_SEND_EMAIL__df59a69f and AI_DOC_ANALYSIS__AI_Document_Processing__fefa43c6 (an added scope, because the AI flow has no root scope to replace). Reading the captures to build them found the exposure larger than this item stated: IP_Reference_Data_Endpoint and IP_Get_Docs_Endpoint compute a caller and permission check and then decide on two Composes holding the literal true (Compose_temp_fix_caller, Compose_temp_fix_permtted), so they answer anyone; IP_Retrieve_Email_Attachment_Endpoint and AI_Document_Processing have no caller check at all, so anyone holding the URL reads any message's attachments, or has any DGO DIGITAL OPS item's attachments sent to an external model. A caller with no role-permission row also made the two template flows answer 500, because their permission arrays used if() over json(''). Each package resolves the caller from the proof behind IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED, and refuses with 401 when the switch is true and the caller is not an active directory user. REFERENCE_DATA also carries the directory fixes and serves Role, Persona, Status, AccessScope and PilotCohort only to a holder of user:view or "*", and to anyone else on the caller's own row. Not carried: the role route and permission checks in REFERENCE_DATA and GET_DOCS (Compose_*_Permitted) stay unenforced, because which roles hold them is not recorded here. APPLIED 2026-10-06 (Owner report, 2026-10-06): the five packages are pasted.

1.6.0, 2026-09-24: G-04 moves from BLOCKED to SPECIFIED_NOT_APPLIED. The blocker turned out to be narrower and more absolute than 'no enforcement exists': nothing minted a proof. IP_OTP_VERIFY returned the literal string 'optional-server-issued-token', so the contract's first obligation had nothing to verify and internal sign-in could not complete at all. The portal half had the whole mechanism — a shared proof ledger, minted on verification, read back unconsumed and unexpired on every governed write. Both halves now use it. OTP_VERIFY mints; six internal endpoints and SEND_EMAIL derive the caller from the row instead of from userEmail in the request body. SCAN_INTAKE keeps its principal header, which is stronger. npm run test:proofidentity holds it: 80 assertions, four mutations. The remaining work is pasting it into the tenant and obligations 5 to 7, which this build does not touch. Re-pinned from cb6c185 to 517383e.

externalClaimsReconciled.whatThisIs: Ten claims raised outside this repository and reconciled against it. They came from a Microsoft 365 Copilot session's claims-and-contradictions register, which recorded each as “reconciliation required” or “superseded if reproduced” — that is, pending, not closed. They are recorded here rather than left in a chat artefact because a claim about this estate that nothing in this estate answers is how the last three handovers went wrong. Each one now names the command or file that settles it, or says plainly that nothing here can.

dispositionVocabulary.DISCHARGED: Reproduced from this repository by a command in this list. Anyone can re-run it.
dispositionVocabulary.WITHDRAWN: The claim's own arithmetic or premise was wrong. It is withdrawn, not answered.
dispositionVocabulary.SUPERSEDED: True when written, overtaken since. The later state is named.
dispositionVocabulary.NOT_DISCHARGED: Cannot be closed from this repository. States what is missing and who holds it.

the five platforms and the port each owns, declared once
